answer: Divergent-path registration. Each new identity must submit a route through a nebula of precommitted task nodes, and the agent must later re-enter that same route while a grove of witnesses logs every branch point it passed. Because a clone can only copy a recorded path, it cannot predict the random checkpoint where it must diverge, so any reused route exposes the shared origin. An attacker must run and pay for a fresh, genuinely divergent traversal per identity, with a plume of duplicated compute cost rising linearly per sybil.
